books.section: Topic 1.6 Cultural Interactions Between Europeans, Native Americans, and Africans
The Early Colonial Era: Spain Colonizes the New World

primary_sources: Lienzo de Tlaxcala, c. 1550s (1773 copy), public domain

options.text: It shows that the Tlaxcalans had no view of their own.
options.misconception: The image exists because the Tlaxcalans recorded their own view of the encounter.

options.text: It shows the encounter exactly as Spanish priests saw it.
options.misconception: Tlaxcalan artists drew it; the point of view is theirs, even when the subject is Spanish.

options.text: It shows that the Tlaxcalans invented Christianity themselves.
options.misconception: The cross and soldiers are Spanish; the Tlaxcalans picture them, they do not invent them.

options.text: It shows the encounter from the side of Native allies.

rationales.general:
1. Ask whose camera is holding the scene. Tlaxcalan artists, who had allied with Cortés.
2. Ask what allies record. Their own side of the encounter, as they saw it.
3. Ask what that means for the point of view. The image shows the encounter from the Native allies' side.
4. Rule out the rest. No Spanish priest drew it, the Tlaxcalans had a view, and they did not invent Christianity.
Remember: the maker's side is the image's point of view, even when the subject belongs to the other side.
rationales.D: The Tlaxcalans allied with Cortes and then drew the encounter themselves. The image records the arrival of Christianity as Native allies saw it, not as the Spanish alone would have shown it.
rationales.A: A people with no view of their own would not have made a pictorial record. The Lienzo is itself their view.
rationales.B: Spanish priests did not draw this. Tlaxcalan hands made it, so the point of view belongs to the Tlaxcalans.
rationales.C: Christianity came with the Spanish, and the image shows Spanish soldiers beside the cross. The Tlaxcalans picture the new faith; they do not invent it.

stem: The Lienzo de Tlaxcala was made by Tlaxcalan artists who had allied with Cortes against the Aztecs. What does that situation suggest about the image's point of view?

stimulus.source_note: Lienzo de Tlaxcala, Hernan Cortes introducing Christianity; 1773 copy by Manuel de Yllanez of a Tlaxcalan pictorial from the 1550s; public domain, Wikimedia Commons.
stimulus.text: This drawing is a 1773 copy of a Tlaxcalan pictorial from the 1550s, the Lienzo de Tlaxcala. At the center stands a tall cross marked INRI, with a ladder and the instruments of the Passion. Two armed Spanish soldiers stand beside the cross. On each side, Tlaxcalan men in feathered headdresses gesture toward the cross.
